A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same eMIGM work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Retained content can be matched reliably despite reflow and additional appendix tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation results, training and sampling ablations, scaling experiments, and masking simulations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds quality metrics, a log-exp masking-schedule experiment, and comparative sampling-time measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix D introduces and evaluates a log-exp masking schedule as an additional training alternative. The main eMIGM architecture, exponential-schedule defaults, diffusion loss, DPM-Solver sampling, and time-interval guidance remain unchanged. The revised CFG-with-Mask description clarifies attribution rather than changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-conditional generation on ImageNet at 256×256 and 512×512. The added metrics, schedule experiment, and timing comparison retain this coverage. Newly cited text-to-image work does not constitute an added evaluated task.

E2.justification: v3 adds EDM2-XXL with Guidance Interval to the ImageNet 512×512 comparison in Table 3 and includes it in the new timing comparison in Table 10. The earlier benchmark comparators are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Table 8 extends benchmark evaluation with sFID, IS, precision, and recall; Table 10 adds comparative timing on one A100 with batch size 256. Tables 2–3 revise the reported REPA budget from 250×2 to 250×1.7 NFEs and EDM2 from 63×2 to 32×2. These are revised reported settings, without evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 9 extends the masking-schedule study with a log-exp alternative, comparing it against linear, cosine, and exponential schedules over 100–400 epochs. The existing architecture, time-truncation, guidance, sampling, and scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10,000 repetitions of the masking simulation in Appendix B.2. Neither adds training-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: The original eMIGM benchmark FIDs are unchanged, but comparative efficiency results change substantially: REPA's reported NFE falls from 500 to 425 and EDM2's from 126 to 64. The added Guidance Interval EDM2 achieves FID 1.40 versus eMIGM-L's 1.77. Tables 8–10 add quality metrics, schedule results, and sampling times of 0.165, 0.552, and 0.481 seconds/image for eMIGM-L, EDM2, and interval-guided EDM2, respectively.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds the mathematical definition gamma_t = log(1 + (exp(5) - 1)t)/5 for the log-exp schedule and discusses schedule boundary conditions. The unified formulation, Equations (1)–(11), and Appendix A's masking-equivalence argument are unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v3 substantially narrows the headline high-resolution claim: v1 claims superiority over state-of-the-art diffusion models using about 60% of their NFEs, whereas v3 claims superiority over the standard EDM2 baseline and emphasizes fewer parameters. The 256×256 claim also changes from below 40% to below 45% of REPA's NFE. The unification, scaling, and VAR-comparison contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges that interval-guided EDM2 achieves better quality and explains eMIGM's faster measured sampling primarily through its smaller parameter count despite higher NFE. It also qualifies transformer-only NFE accounting with approximately 14% additional MLP overhead and motivates log-exp masking as balancing extreme mask ratios.

D1.justification: v3 announces eMIGM code availability and supplies a project code link absent from v1. It newly discloses transformer-only NFE accounting and specifies the hardware and batch size for the added cost measurements. Existing tokenizer specifications, implementation sources, and training-configuration tables are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations for Meissonic, AdaNAT, HART, CADS, guidance-weight schedulers, and masked-transformer inference improvements. It explicitly identifies CFG with Mask as an adaptation of Nie et al.'s text-generation approach and more carefully relates its scheduling observations to prior work. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the abstract, weighting-function explanation, CFG attribution, efficiency discussion, and related work, plus additional Appendix D paragraphs. Affiliations and publication text change, and acknowledgements are added. The main section sequence and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 8–10, expands Table 3 with a comparator row and explanatory marker, and revises comparison captions. Figure 4 moves from page 6 to page 7, with accompanying text reflow. All eight original figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical transparency by correcting baseline NFE counts, qualifying the EDM2 claim, disclosing omitted MLP cost, and adding common-hardware timing and broader quality metrics. These benefits outweigh a localized new reporting error: the claim that eMIGM-B outperforms StyleGAN-XL conflicts with Table 2's FIDs of 2.32 versus 2.30. The main experimental results and theoretical argument otherwise remain stable.
